newsitem.title: USA: Crown, union return to bargaining table.
newsitem.headline: Crown, union return to bargaining table.

text.p: Crown Central Petroleum Corp and union negotiators were set to return to the bargaining table on Tuesday to resume talks on a new labor pact for workers at the company's Texas refinery.

The two sides met with a federal mediator in a day-long session on Friday aimed at ending the 10-month lockout at the 100,000 barrel per day Pasadena, Texas refinery, but made little progress on two key issues, a union spokesman said.
"I don't think we made a lot of progress," said Joe Campbell, head of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Local 4-227, which represents 225 Crown refinery workers.
The union rejected a proposal that would allow Baltimore-based Crown to replace 40 percent of its workers with contractors and ignore seniority in determining which workers remain on the job.

"It seems like there's a meaningful dialogue, and that's positive," said Crown spokesman Joe Coale, who declined to comment in detail about the talks. "We're still talking, and while we're talking that's positive."
The labor dispute began on February 5 when union workers were locked out after some equipment was vandalized. The refinery is being operated by management and contractors.
